title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous pages. K is a field finitely generated over Q, with absolute transcendence degree n. K_0 is the algebraic closure of Q in K, a number field. Writing E for Grothendieck's script E, there is an exact sequence (8):
1 → Π_{K̄/K} → E_{K̄/K} → Γ → 1.
Here E_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/K) is the absolute Galois group, Π_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/K·Q̄) is the geometric part, and Γ = Gal(Q̄/K_0) is an open subgroup of Γ_Q.

This sequence is the projective limit, over a cofinal system of smooth models U_i of K (Artin's 'grandes' elementary neighbourhoods), of the homotopy exact sequences 1 → π_i = π_1(Ū_i) → E_i = π_1(U_i) → Γ → 1. Each π_i is a successive extension of n free profinite groups, being the profinite completion of the π_1 of an Artin elementary fibration.

Cohomological dimension. From this structure:
- cd π_i = n.
- cd_ℓ E_i ≤ n + cd_ℓ Γ = n+2 for odd torsion coefficients.
Passing to the limit (cohomology commutes with projective limits of profinite groups) gives (14):
- cd Π_{K̄/K} ≤ n;
- cd_ℓ E_{K̄/K} ≤ n+2 for every prime ℓ ≠ 2.
Grothendieck adds that these are in fact equalities ('sauf erreur'). This gives a purely cohomological characterisation of the absolute transcendence degree: n = cd Π = cd_ℓ(G_K) − 2 for ℓ odd.

Theorem 1. For K finitely generated over Q, every open subgroup of G_K = E_{K̄/K} has trivial centralizer in G_K. The same holds for Π_{K̄/K}. In modern language, these groups are 'slim'.

Strategy of proof, begun here and continued on the next page:
1. Let E' ⊂ E be open. Its image Γ' in Γ is open, hence open in Γ_Q.
2. The centralizer Z of E' maps into the centralizer of Γ' in Γ_Q.
3. Corollary (next page): in Γ_Q the centralizer of any open subgroup is trivial. Reduce to Γ' open normal. Its center is trivial ('bien connu (?)'). So the centralizer Z injects into the finite group Γ_Q/Γ' and is finite. By Artin–Schreier, the only nontrivial torsion elements are conjugates of complex conjugation τ. The centralizer of τ is {1,τ}, which cannot contain the open Γ'. Hence Z = 1.
4. Therefore Z ⊂ Π, and Z centralizes the open subgroup Π' = E'∩Π of Π. One is reduced to slimness of Π. That should follow from Π being built from free profinite groups of rank ≥ 2; the next page breaks off before this.
errors: Not an error but a hedge Grothendieck flags himself: the center-freeness of open normal subgroups of Γ_Q is asserted as 'bien connu (?)' without proof. It is true (it follows from Hilbertianity, or from local–global arguments à la Neukirch), but it is the real content of the corollary.

The exclusion ℓ ≠ 2 is necessary and correctly made: when K_0 has real places, cd_2 G_K = ∞. The equality claims (cd Π = n, cd_ℓ G_K = n+2 for ℓ odd) are correct; cf. Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne II §4.
On this page the proof of Theorem 1 is incomplete. It breaks off after reducing to the image in Γ, and the reduction to slimness of Π is only begun on the next page.

ideas.what: Profinite fundamental groups of Artin good neighbourhoods are successive extensions of free profinite groups; the geometric Galois group of a function field is the limit of these.
ideas.modern_name: Artin elementary fibrations / good K(π,1) neighbourhoods
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 XI (Artin), used in SGA context

ideas.what: cd Π_{K̄/K} = n and cd_ℓ G_K = n+2 (ℓ odd) for K finitely generated over Q of transcendence degree n, so the transcendence degree is recovered cohomologically from the Galois group.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological dimension of function fields (Tsen–Lang / Serre)
ideas.where_published: Serre CG II.4.2; the group-theoretic recovery of tr.deg is standard in anabelian geometry (Pop)

ideas.what: Open subgroups of G_K (K finitely generated over Q), of Π_{K̄/K} and of G_Q have trivial centralizers. Proof via Artin–Schreier: torsion in G_Q is only complex conjugations, which are self-centralizing.
ideas.modern_name: Slimness of absolute Galois groups (Mochizuki's term 'slim')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Neukirch, Ikeda, Fried–Jarden (Hilbertian fields), Nakamura (~1990), Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Not explicitly in the Esquisse or Longue Marche as published, to my knowledge. It appears in the anabelian literature (Nakamura 1990, Mochizuki 1990s).

missed.claim: An early, apparently early-1980s formulation by Grothendieck of the 'slimness' of G_K and of the geometric Galois group, as a preliminary step in his anabelian programme. It predates the explicit treatments by Nakamura and Mochizuki, but the result itself is known and is attributed to others.
missed.quote: Alors pour tout sous-groupe ouvert E de E_{K̄/K}, son centralisateur dans E_{K̄/K} est réduit au groupe unité. Item pour Π_{K̄/K}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical only: it documents that Grothendieck identified slimness as a basic ingredient of the anabelian setup. It adds no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains standard results: cohomological dimension of Galois groups of finitely generated fields, and the triviality of centralizers of open subgroups. These are well known and credited to Serre, Artin, Neukirch, Nakamura and others. The only interest is historical, as an early instance of the slimness property in Grothendieck's anabelian notes.
transcription_corrections: The label of the displayed inequalities is probably '(14)', continuing the numbering (12), (13) of the previous page, rather than '(K)'.
'par p.s.r.g' is probably an abbreviation for 'par passage à la limite' (the reading is uncertain).
Insertion above 'de type fini': 'extension de type fini de Q'.
Struck-out passages at the bottom: 'L'image dans Γ des centralis. de E ... centralise Γ'...' are crossed out; the final retained text is 'Je dis qu'il est [égale à 1]'.
